kept.title: Unsafe Dynamic Code Execution (New Function)
kept.description: The `HandlerStorage` class generates and compiles JavaScript function strings using `new Function()` with dynamically built bodies derived from user-defined route parameters and constraints.
steps_to_exploit: Define a route parameter name containing malicious JS syntax (e.g., 'x');constructor('eval(name)')()').
Trigger the router's compilation mechanism for that route.
The router evaluates the string in the constructor context, leading to arbitrary code execution.
kept.impact: Full Remote Code Execution (RCE) on the server process.

kept.title: Prototype Pollution via NullObject/Constructor
kept.description: The `_createParamsObject` method in `lib/handler-storage.js` builds objects using a custom `NullObject` constructor, but the dynamic property assignment `params['${params[i]}']` is vulnerable if `params[i]` contains prototype-accessing keys like `__proto__` or `constructor`.
steps_to_exploit: Create a route with a parameter name like 'constructor' or '__proto__'.
Lookup a path that maps to this parametric route.
The router sets properties on the result object, which overwrites prototype properties for the entire application.
kept.impact: Global state modification, potentially leading to denial of service or privilege escalation.

kept.title: Denial of Service via ReDoS in RegExp Compilation
kept.description: The router compiles user-provided regular expressions from route definitions using `new RegExp()`. While `safe-regex2` is used for check, it is not exhaustive against advanced ReDoS vectors in complex groups.
steps_to_exploit: Register a route with a regex that passes simple safety checks but is complex enough to trigger backtracking.
Send a request path that causes the engine to perform exponential backtracking in the regex engine.
The Event Loop is blocked, causing service unavailability.
kept.impact: Resource exhaustion and total application Denial of Service.

kept.title: Improper Input Validation of Route Constraints
kept.description: The `Constrainer` allows users to define custom constraints, but `addConstraintStrategy` does not properly sanitize or limit the naming of constraints, potentially conflicting with reserved internal keys.
steps_to_exploit: Register a custom constraint with the name 'version' or 'host'.
The logic in `constrainer.js` and `handler-storage.js` may behave unpredictably by overriding internal logic with the custom strategy.
This leads to incorrect handler selection or routing logic bypassing.
kept.impact: Security logic bypasses and potential for misrouting requests.

kept.title: Sync/Async Constraint Race Conditions
kept.description: Constraints can be either synchronous or asynchronous. The `deriveAsyncConstraints` method performs multiple asynchronous lookups concurrently, but the implementation does not guarantee the order or atomicity of constraint resolution.
steps_to_exploit: Define multiple async constraints.
Simulate high-concurrency requests.
The `asyncConstraintsCount` counter might be susceptible to race conditions if the `deriveAsyncConstraints` loop is misused, leading to incomplete or incorrect context matching.
kept.impact: Authentication or authorization bypass if constraint evaluation fails or provides inconsistent data.

kept.title: Integer Overflow in Bitmask Logic
kept.description: The router uses a bitmask (31 bits) to match handlers. If more than 31 handlers are assigned to a single node, the system explicitly throws an error, but the logic relies on `1 << i`, which in JavaScript treats operands as 32-bit signed integers.
steps_to_exploit: Register exactly 32 handlers to a node that supports constraints.
The bitmask logic will overflow the signed bit, resulting in invalid handler index mapping.
The router may return an incorrect handler or `null` even if a match exists.
kept.impact: Routing errors and unreliable handler selection.

kept.title: Insecure Error Handling in `safeDecodeURI`
kept.description: The `safeDecodeURI` function swallows errors and returns `null` or falls back to an `onBadUrl` handler without sufficiently validating the input for malicious character sequences.
steps_to_exploit: Send a request with malformed percent-encoding.
The exception is caught and passed to `onBadUrl`.
If the `onBadUrl` handler does not strictly validate the input, malicious payloads can be echoed or processed by downstream logic.
kept.impact: XSS or injection potential via improperly handled error paths.

kept.title: Bypassing Authentication via Constraint Mismatch
kept.description: The `mustMatchWhenDerived` logic in `HandlerStorage` assumes that if a constraint is derived but missing from the route, it should return null. This is highly fragile and depends on every custom constraint implementing this logic correctly.
steps_to_exploit: Create a constraint where the developer fails to implement `mustMatchWhenDerived` correctly.
Send a request containing the constraint header.
The router fails to reject the request and matches a handler that shouldn't be accessible.

kept.title: Lack of Memory Limit on Route Storage
kept.description: The router does not limit the number of routes that can be added to the internal `routes` array or the complexity of the radix tree.
steps_to_exploit: Dynamically register an extremely large number of routes with long, unique, or complex paths.
The heap usage of the Node.js process grows until it crashes.
kept.impact: Denial of Service via memory exhaustion.

kept.title: Unintended Exposure of Internal Meta-Data
kept.description: The `prettyPrint` function and `defaultBuildPrettyMeta` expose the internal `store` objects of routes, which may contain sensitive application configuration, database schemas, or internal metadata.
steps_to_exploit: Call the `prettyPrint()` method if exposed via an admin route or logs.
The entire internal structure and associated metadata are rendered into a string.
kept.impact: Information disclosure of internal application structure.

kept.title: Path Traversal via Normalized URL
kept.description: The `removeDuplicateSlashes` and `trimLastSlash` utilities are applied after path decoding in some branches, potentially allowing path traversal if the user-defined `defaultRoute` or custom handlers use the path for filesystem lookups.
steps_to_exploit: Send a request like `/static/../secret/file`.
The router might normalize the path incorrectly depending on the sequence of normalization steps.
kept.impact: Unauthorized access to files or directories.

kept.title: Inconsistent Case Sensitivity Handling
kept.description: If `caseSensitive` is disabled, the router forces all paths to lowercase. This can lead to security bypasses if authorization rules are case-sensitive but the routing is not.
steps_to_exploit: Register a restricted path `/Admin`.
Send a request to `/admin`.
The router matches the path, but downstream security middleware might not recognize it as the protected `/Admin` endpoint.

kept.title: ReDoS via Regex Param Extraction
kept.description: The `getClosingParenthensePosition` helper function uses a manual loop to find the end of a regex group. If a very deeply nested or malformed regex string is provided, it can be extremely slow.
steps_to_exploit: Provide a route definition with deeply nested regex parentheses.
The router takes significant time during initialization to parse the regex, blocking the event loop.
kept.impact: Denial of Service during application startup or route registration.

kept.title: Weak Randomness/Uniqueness in Constraints
kept.description: The `ConstraintStrategy` implementation relies on user-provided strings for keys, which are not namespaced, leading to high collision probability if multiple plugins use the same constraint key.
steps_to_exploit: Register two different plugins that both use the 'version' or 'custom' constraint key.
The router will cause one plugin to overwrite the other's routing logic.
kept.impact: Unpredictable behavior and security configuration conflicts.

kept.title: Hardcoded Node Version Requirement
kept.description: The router requires Node >= 20. Running in an older environment may cause subtle bugs in modern JS features (like `Object.hasOwn` or `RegExp` features) which are assumed to exist.
steps_to_exploit: Run the router in an environment slightly below Node 20.
The lack of polyfills for modern features might lead to silent failures where security checks (like `hasOwn`) do nothing.
kept.impact: Security bypasses due to feature failure in unsupported environments.
